title: Show existing customers what new customers pay, and stop charging them more at renewal
action: Publish the interest rates lenders are offering new borrowers so existing borrowers can compare, require insurance renewal notices to show last year's premium and the change, and consider the UK rule that a renewal price can be no higher than the price offered to an equivalent new customer.
why: Charging loyal customers more than new ones weakens competition: firms win customers with low introductory prices and recover them from those who do not switch, so overall prices stay higher.

evidence.source: Competition in the Australian Financial System
evidence.quote: APRA should continuously collect data from mortgage lenders (authorised deposittaking institutions (ADIs) only) on interest rates of new residential home loans by borrower and loan characteristics.

evidence.source: Competition in the Australian Financial System
evidence.quote: Renewal notices for general insurance products should transparently include the previous year's premium and the percentage change to the new premium.

evidence.source: PS21/5: General insurance pricing practices market study, Feedback to CP20/19 and final rules
evidence.quote: A pricing remedy requiring that when a firm offers a renewal price to a customer, this should be no greater than the equivalent new business price (ENBP) for a new customer.

precedents.what: Banned 'price walking' in home and motor insurance from January 2022: renewal prices may not exceed the price for an equivalent new customer.
